newsitem.title: KENYA: Nairobi bourse shares down in tense Kenya.
newsitem.headline: Nairobi bourse shares down in tense Kenya.

text.p: The Nairobi Stock Exchange shares slumped on Wednesday dragged down by cautious traders wary of rising tension sparked by opposition calls for constitutional reforms, brokers and bourse officials said.
The 20-share index was down 22.21 points to close at 3535.72. Turnover was posted at 7.6 million shillings traded on 267,970 shares compared to 33.9 million shillings on 383,263 shares on Tuesday.
"It was slow trading -- a very flat session all the way. Most of the trading was done across books," a bourse official said.
Brokers said an outbreak of violence in the country from pro-reform protestors on Monday had paralysed business including the stock exchange.
"We had nothing to sell today. Most of the orders were stuck at the registrars on Monday and we've lost about two days of business," a senior broker said.
They said foreign investors who for the last month had hyped up sentiment at the market were notably quiet.
They traded Kenya Commercial Bank at 107 from 108 and East Africa Portland Cement at 40.25 from 40.
Barclays Bank was unchanged at 111 while National Industrial Credit Bank closed at 46 from 64.50.
Brooke Bond shed two shillings to close at 122 while Rea Vipingo Plantations eased to 10.15 from 10.20.
Kenya Power & Lighting eased to 172 from 173 while Total Kenya shed a shilling to close at 65 from 64.
Uchumi Supermarket closed at 38.25 from 38 while Nation Printers & Publishers was unchanged at 115. Kenya Airways eased to 8.20 from 8.25.
